title: European tour cut short by Covid in March 2020
summary: Sportiello describes underestimating the virus, concert cancellations on his Feb-April tour, last gig on March 13 in Germany and the flight home on March 16.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well you know I have to tell you I was never much technological and I’m still not technological. But I was not into social medias. I believed as far as I’m healthy and I keep practicing I could go places to play music. And nobody would have ever guessed that something like this would happen. At least it was far away. You know unfortunately I was one of those guys that when this mess started to happen that we were hearing about it in February and very early March, I thought that they were making it bigger than what it really was, and of course I was wrong. So I never thought that after thirty years of performing live with a full schedule — thirty years — I never thought that we could get to a stop like this. You know?
Yeah. And it’s across the board, you know people who are NEA Jazz Masters can’t get a gig as well as the people who are playing in the American Legion on the weekends. It’s the same for everybody.

Yeah. Yeah, and so what happened, I was on tour in Europe. The tour started at the end of February and was supposed to go on until the first week of April. All one nighters, you know? But of course at around March 8, 9, 10, we started being bombarded with emails of people cancelling our concerts. And so our last performance was actually on March 13 in Germany.
